name: Cyrus decrees that the exiles may return and rebuild the temple
summary: In his first year as king of Persia, Cyrus issues a decree permitting the Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple of the LORD, urging their neighbors to support them with gifts.

name: Cyrus returns the temple's sacred vessels through Sheshbazzar
summary: Cyrus brings out the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the LORD's house and hands them over to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah, to carry back to Jerusalem.

name: The exiles who return to Judah are numbered under Zerubbabel and Jeshua
summary: Ezra records the roster of families and towns among those who return from Babylon to Judah and Jerusalem, led by Zerubbabel and Jeshua, numbering the whole assembly at 42,360.

name: The returned exiles rebuild the altar and resume the prescribed sacrifices
summary: Zerubbabel and Jeshua lead the people in rebuilding the altar on its old foundations and resuming the burnt offerings and the Feast of Booths despite their fear of the surrounding peoples.

name: The temple's foundation is laid amid joy and weeping
summary: When the temple's foundation is laid, the priests and Levites praise the LORD while many of the older exiles who remembered the first temple weep aloud, so joy and weeping mix into one great noise.

name: Rejected adversaries discourage and frighten the builders
summary: The peoples of the land, refused a share in building the temple after offering to help, hire counselors against the returned exiles and frighten them so the work stalls through the reign of Cyrus into that of Darius.

name: Haggai and Zechariah prompt Zerubbabel and Jeshua to resume building
summary: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua respond by resuming construction on the temple despite the earlier royal order to stop.

name: Tattenai questions the builders' authority and writes to Darius
summary: Tattenai, governor of the province beyond the Euphrates, asks the builders who authorized their work, then sends a letter to King Darius asking him to search the records for Cyrus's decree.

name: Darius finds Cyrus's decree and orders the temple fully funded
summary: A search of the royal archives turns up Cyrus's original decree, and Darius orders Tattenai to let the work continue and to pay its full cost from the royal revenue, threatening severe punishment for interference.

name: The temple is completed and dedicated with great joy
summary: The temple is finished in the sixth year of Darius's reign, and the people, priests, and Levites dedicate it with a joyful sacrifice of bulls, rams, lambs, and goats.

name: The returned exiles celebrate the Passover
summary: Having purified themselves, the returned exiles keep the Passover together and celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, because the LORD had turned the king's heart toward them.

name: Ezra, a scribe skilled in the Law, prepares to return to Jerusalem
summary: Decades after the temple's completion, Ezra the priest, a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, sets his heart to study and teach the LORD's law and sets out from Babylon for Jerusalem in the reign of Artaxerxes.

name: Artaxerxes' letter authorizes Ezra's mission and provides resources
summary: King Artaxerxes grants Ezra a letter authorizing him to lead any willing exiles back to Jerusalem, appoint judges, teach the law, and carry gold and silver for the temple's service.

name: The family heads who return with Ezra are listed
summary: Ezra records the family heads and the number of men who register to travel with him from Babylon to Jerusalem, discovering along the way that no Levites had yet joined the group.

name: Ezra proclaims a fast before the journey, ashamed to request soldiers
summary: Ashamed to ask King Artaxerxes for soldiers to protect the group after telling him the LORD's hand favors those who seek him, Ezra proclaims a fast at the river Ahava to seek a safe journey.

name: Ezra's group arrives safely in Jerusalem with the temple's treasures
summary: The group travels from the Ahava to Jerusalem, arriving safely after four months, and the silver, gold, and vessels entrusted to the priests are weighed out and found to match exactly.

name: Ezra learns the people have intermarried with surrounding peoples
summary: Officials report to Ezra that the people, including priests and Levites, have not separated themselves from the surrounding peoples but have intermarried with them, against the Law's command.

name: Ezra prays a confession of the nation's guilt
summary: Appalled, Ezra tears his garment, falls to his knees, and prays aloud, confessing that the nation's guilt for this unfaithfulness has again risen higher than their heads before God.

name: Shecaniah proposes a covenant to put away foreign wives
summary: As a great assembly weeps with Ezra, Shecaniah proposes that Israel make a covenant with God to send away the foreign wives and children, and urges Ezra to take courage and act.

name: The men who had married foreign wives are listed
summary: After the assembly agrees to Shecaniah's proposal and investigates case by case, Ezra records the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and other Israelites who had married foreign women.
